project.name: Personalized vision-driven adaptive canine below-knee prosthesis — Dog G
project.model_type: 2D sagittal nonlinear hybrid time-domain forward dynamics; vision-driven proximal motion, dynamic paw-compression DOF, literature-calibrated stance loading, and finite stiffness-actuator dynamics
project.reference_frame: subject-specific knee-centered coordinates from Dog G vision trajectories

geometry.source: Dog G median per-stride marker geometry from the processed Catavitello trajectories

segment_inertia_proxy.source: Ragetly normalized Labrador segment-property proxies scaled to Dog G body mass; not CAD mass properties

spring_damper.notes: Neutral hock angle derived directly from Dog G stance kinematics; damping remains fixed engineering initialization.

stiffness_bounds.basis: Subject-scaled compliant design space for Dog G. k_calf upper bound scales with body mass under the same 5-degree flexibility criterion; k_paw remains broad effective prosthetic compliance.
stiffness_bounds.warning: Preliminary results reach the current 10 kN/m lower bound for k_paw in the global static baseline and trot adaptive case. These are not final stiffness values; add loading/GRF constraints before thesis-level calibration.

actuator_dynamics.notes: Fixed first-order stiffness-transition dynamics. Replace with measured hardware response time when an actuator/mechanism is selected.

simulation.notes: Optimization uses 180 RK4 steps/cycle; final reporting is rerun at 600 steps/cycle.

contact_plausibility.notes: Soft plausibility limits for reduced-order compliance states; these are not measured biological limits.

load_bearing_support.method: For each gait, derive a fixed support-mass fraction and a fixed acceleration gain so the ideal stance load-demand profile matches BOTH the independent published pelvic-limb peak vertical force and vertical impulse.
load_bearing_support.notes: The load-demand profile uses the shape of the vision-derived hock vertical acceleration, but its peak and mean are calibrated to independent GRF literature. These load parameters are fixed and are not optimization variables.

walk.source: Torres et al./Vet Comp Orthop Traumatol walking force-platform study in heterogeneous orthopedically normal dogs: mean pelvic PVF 38.66% BW and VI 13.96 %BW*s at preferred relative walking velocity.
walk.population_note: 17 orthopedically normal heterogeneous dogs; normalized values are used as population-level load constraints, not synchronized measurements for the vision dogs.

trot.source: Ragetly et al. 2010 healthy Labrador pelvic limbs at trot: PVF 6.32 N/kg = 64.5% BW, VI 0.89 Ns/kg = 9.1 %BW*s.
trot.population_note: Healthy Labrador retrievers at ~1.98 m/s; normalized values are used as population-level load constraints.

contact_geometry.basis: Fixed reduced-order center-of-pressure lever arm. The resultant vertical ground reaction is applied at 40% of the hock-to-toe length rather than at the toe tip. This avoids the unrealistically large hock moment created by a full-toe lever arm. It is an engineering proxy, not a measured COP location.

hock_moment_plausibility.basis: Conservative soft upper envelope for healthy canine tarsal/hock net moment at trot. It is used only as a soft plausibility penalty, not as a point target.

flexibility_constraint.interpretation: Engineering design constraint for a flexible prosthesis; not biological stiffness.
